title: December 3, 2026 BZA Agenda
text: Augusta County Board of Zoning Appeals BZA Regular Meeting Thursday, December 3, 2026 – 1:30 PM Augusta County Government Center Main Board Room 18 Government Center Lane Verona, VA 24482 1. Call to Order 2. Determination of Quorum 3. Minutes a. 4. Approval of the November 5, 2026 Minutes Public Hearing a. A request by Walda R. Massie, for a Special Use Permit to amend the operating conditions for Special Use Permit #24-47 to meet the requirements of Augusta Water on property she owns located at 153 Drifting Lane, Waynesboro in the Middle River District. b. A request by Jeremiah Jenkins, agent for Song Bird House, LLC, for a Special Use Permit to operate a short term rental on property owned by Song Bird House, LLC located at 1292 Natural Chimneys Road, Mount Solon in the North River District. c. A request by Dennis Dwayne Miller, for a Special Use Permit to construct a dwelling to be used as a short term rental on property he owns located at the end of Poor Creek Lane, east of the intersection of Lee Highway (Route 11) and Poor Creek Lane in the Riverheads District. d. A request by Benjamin R. Gee, for a Special Use Permit to lease office space within the existing building and to place a pre-fab building for storage on property he owns located at 2986 Churchville Avenue, Staunton in the Pastures District. e. A request by Charles Benjamin and Rebecca Roche Pickin, for a Special Use Permit to have a dog kennel for personal dogs on property they own located at 4577 Rockfish Road, Grottoes in the Middle River District. f. A request by Sam Yowres, agent for Augusta CSG 2, LLC, for a Special Use Permit to construct a small scale solar facility on approximately 24.7 acres on properties owned by Ebco II, LLC and Rebb, LLC located on the north side of Parkersburg Turnpike (Route 254) across from the Cedar Green Subdivision and less than one (1) mile from the City of Staunton in the Pastures District. g. A request by Benjamin Gillespie, agent for Summit Ridge Energy, LLC for a Special Use Permit to construct a small scale solar facility on property owned by South River Farms, LLC located at 1749 Weyers Cave Road, Grottoes in the Middle River District. 5. Old Business a. A request by Jared Perry, for a Special Use Permit to have a small engine and equipment repair business on property owned by David W. and Sherri M. Perry 50% and Ronald M. McKee, Etal located at 218 Dooms Crossing Road, Waynesboro in the Middle River District. - Reconsider screening requirements for SUP#26-60 6. Matters to Be Presented by the Public 7. Matters to Be Presented by the Zoning Administrator a. A request by Mark Kincaid, for a Special Use Permit to continue to have motor vehicle and tractor repair in a larger structure on the property and to relocate the impoundment area on property he owns located at 1870 Calf Mountain Road, Waynesboro in the Wayne District. - One (1) Year Extension of Time Request b. A request by Brian Manley, agent for Valley Contracting, LLC, for a Special Use Permit to have a construction/excavating and hauling business with outdoor storage of commercial vehicles and equipment on property owned by Crosby Farm, LLC located at 436 Hankey Mountain Highway, Churchville in the Pastures District. - Nine (9) Month Extension of Time Request c. A request by Melinda Kendell, agent for Cider House Farm, LLC, for a Special Use Permit to have a food prep kitchen within the tasting room of the cidery in order to prepare and sell food on property owned by Cider House Farm, LLC, located on the southeast side of Route 640 (Old White Bridge Road), adjacent to 949 Old White Bridge Road in the Wayne District. - Six (6) Month Extension of Time Request d. A request by Craig Williams, agent for the Churchville Volunteer Fire Department, for a Special Use Permit to enlarge and extend an existing nonconforming structure on property it owns, located at 3829 Churchville Avenue, Churchville, in the Pastures District. - Two (2) Year Extension of Time Request 8. title: Meeting Packet
text: Practical Law for Civic Leaders Implementation of the Retail Cannabis Marketplace in Virginia Webinar: September 16, 2026 Maxwell C. Hlavin, Esquire, Sands Anderson PC Elizabeth S. Chupik, Esquire, Sands Anderson PC Rebecca J. Powers, Esquire, Sands Anderson PC Donnie Autry, Esquire, County of Arlington Part 1: What changed Budget Bill Overview Timeline License Types Role of VCCA 2 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC 2026 Special Session Budget Bill (HB30) Establishes a regulated, adult-use commercial cannabis market in Virginia, building on the Commonwealth’s 2021 legalization of personal possession and limited home cultivation 3 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Vests the Virginia Cannabis Control Authority (“VCCA”) and its Board of Directors (“Board”) with plenary power to license, regulate, tax, and enforce all commercial cannabis, cannabis product, and regulated hemp product activity in Virginia Amends and reenacts numerous existing Virginia Code provisions, including the Cannabis Control Act framework in Title 4.1 2026 Special Session Budget Bill Overview Imposes a state tax of 6% (rising to 8% on and after July 1, 2029) in addition to Retail Sales and Use Tax, and a mandatory local tax of 1% to 3.5%; and 4 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Limits the role of localities to local taxation, zoning and land use, hours of sale, and public consumption/buffer ordinances, while preempting contrary local regulations Timeline Certain hemp-related amendments take effect Deadline for Board to adopt implementing regulation Board may begin issuing licenses Virginia Cannabis Control Authority (“VCCA”) may begin accepting license applications 15 Aug. 2026 5 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC 1 Feb. 2027 1 May 2027 Majority of licensing, criminal, and enforcement provisions take effect 1 July 2027 State tax increase from 6% to 8% 1 July 2029 2026 Special Session Budget Bill Overview Possession Limit Increased: Legal to possess up to 2 ounces of cannabis (§ 4.1-1100(A)) Public consumption penalties increase on 7/1/2027 (§ 4.1-1108) • In-home cultivation of up to 4 plants remains unchanged • 1st Offense from $25 to $250; • 2nd Offense: $250 fine & Substance Abuse Program; • 3rd & Subsequent Offense: Class 4 Misdemeanor Banking access authorized (§ 6.2108) Cannabis Equity Reinvestment Fund (§ 2.2-2499.8) & Equity Business Loan Fund (§ 4.1-1501) established 6 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC VCCA jurisdiction expanded: sole regulator of cannabis (§§ 4.11700-1704) Repeals industrial hemp provisions (Art. 4, § § 3.2-4122 to 4126, 3.2-5145.4:1, 4.1-1101.1, 4.1-1105.1, 18.2-248.1 & 18.2251.1) Licenses: Cultivation Marijuana Cultivation Facilities: authorizes cultivation and packaging of marijuana and marijuana products • Tier I - Up to 5,000 SF Canopy • Tier II - Up to 10,000 SF Canopy • Tier III - Up to 15,000 SF Canopy, Indoor Only • Tier IV - Up to 25,000 SF Canopy, Indoor Only • Tier V - Up to 35,000 SF Canopy, Indoor Only 7 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Microbusiness: authorizes a combination of cultivation, processing, and retail activities; limits cultivation (5,000 SF canopy indoors and 10,000 SF canopy outdoors) Licenses: Processing and Testing Marijuana Processing Facility: authorizes the processing, labeling, packaging, and transport of marijuana, as well as sale to retail stores and other processing facilities Marijuana Testing Facility: authorizes development, research, transport, and testing of marijuana Pharmaceutical Processer/Cannabis Dispensing Facility: authorizes the cultivation, processing, and distribution of cannabis products to registered patients under the medical cannabis program 8 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Licenses: Transport and Sale Retail Marijuana Store: authorizes the sale of marijuana and marijuana products directly to consumers; capped at 2,500 SF Marijuana Delivery Operator: authorizes the permit holder to take possession from retail stores and microbusinesses and deliver them only in person to consumers Marijuana Transporter: authorizes the permit holder to take possession from cultivation facilities, processing facilities, retail stores, microbusinesses, and other transporters; no direct interaction with consumers. 9 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC License Caps Tier V Cultivation Licenses: Capped at 5 before January 1, 2028 Microbusiness Licenses: 100 reserved for industrial hemp processors/growers, qualifying impact licensees, and USDAqualified farmers before May 1, 2027 At least 55 additional Licenses must be issued by July 1, 2027 Cultivation/Processing licenses for industrial hemp growers or processors: Capped at 20, with no more than 10 cultivation licenses and no more than 10 processing, by May 1, 2027 10 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part II: What Localities Cannot Do 11 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Virginia Code § 4.1-629(A): State Preemption “No county, city or town shall, except as provided in §4.1-630, adopt any ordinance or resolution that regulates or prohibits the cultivation, processing, possession, sale, distribution, handling, transportation, consumption, use, advertising, or dispensing of marijuana or marijuana products.” 12 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Localities may NOT: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 Ban or “opt out” of the cannabis marketplace Impose moratoriums on cannabis business operations Regulate advertising of cannabis or cannabis products Regulate possession limits, product types, potency, or packaging Cap the number of licenses within their boundaries Increase the VCCA Board’s minimum distance/buffer requirements Impose any tax other than the 13.5% local tax 13 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part III: What Localities Must Do 14 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Cannabis Tax Decisions [§ 4.1-1004(B)(1)] • Local cannabis tax rate may not be less than 1% and may not be more than 3.5% • The effective date of any such ordinance is the first day of the second month following the ordinance enactment • Once set, the rate must stay in place for three years 15 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Deadline for Locality Action: No fixed statutory deadline, but must be in place prior to the start of retail cannabis sales on July 1, 2027 Tax Revenue Tax Rate $1M in Retail Sales 1% $10,000 2% $20,000 3.5% $35,000 16 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Cannabis Tax Actions 1 2 3 4 Notify the VCCA within 30 days (§ 4.11004(B)(1)) Notify retail cannabis stores and microbusinesses in the locality within 30 days (§ 4.1-1004(B)(1)) Publish notice of the proposed tax (§ 58.13007) Hold a public hearing before enacting/increasing the local tax (§ 58.13007) 17 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Cannabis Tax for Towns Note: County tax rates do NOT apply within the limits of any town located therein Towns must independently levy their own local cannabis tax Towns that fail to act will have no local tax revenue from cannabis sales occurring within the corporate limits 18 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Adopt Internal Administrative Procedures [§§ 4.1-1000(G), 4.1-810] Localities will receive communications from the VCCA related to preliminary approvals of licenses by the VCCA in their locality Localities should adopt procedures for receiving and responding to such communications Failure to file a formal objection to any such notification within 30 days automatically waives the locality’s objection to the approval Recommend designation of locality staff for monitoring of CCA communications and drafting a form objection letter for future use Deadline for Locality Action: none, but the sooner the better 19 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part IV: What Localities May Do 20 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Review Code Conflicts [§ 4.1-629(D) Localities should review their local ordinances to confirm there are no conflicts or inconsistencies with the new state law governing cannabis Identify conflicting local provisions that need repeal or amendment to comply with the new state law Deadline for Locality Action: Start this process with staff; referral to the Planning Commission 21 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Zoning, Land Use, & Business Licenses [§ 4.1-629(C)] Localities retain substantial authority regarding zoning, land use, and business-license requirements, subject to the limitations and preemption provisions of the VCCA. Localities should review and update their local zoning ordinances to provide regulation of cannabis businesses Zoning and land use regulation represent a significant tool for localities to regulate cannabis-related uses in their borders VCCA may deny final licenses if the establishment violates zoning (§ 4.1-1000(H)(3)) 22 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Local Zoning Tools/Options Designating zoning districts for specific cannabis-related uses Requiring conditional use permits or special exceptions – with potential risk Site plan requirements Setback and buffer distances – which may be decreased but not increased from VCCA Board minimums, which are TBD Deadline for Locality Action: Should be in place by May 1, 2027, or sooner 23 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Public Consumption Ordinances Permitted § 4.1-629(B)(1) LOCALITIES MAY ADOPT ORDINANCES PROHIBITING THE ACTS DESCRIBED IN § 4.1-1108 (PUBLIC CONSUMPTION) AND § 4.1-1109 (POSSESSION/CONSUMPTION ON PUBLIC SCHOOL GROUNDS) IN LOCAL PUBLIC PARKS, PLAYGROUNDS, STREETS, OR SIDEWALKS ADJACENT TO ANY PUBLIC STREET LOCAL ORDINANCE MAY PRESCRIBE PENALTY FOR VIOLATIONS, BUT PROVIDES NO MAXIMUM OR MINIMUM PENALTY Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 24 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Buffer Reductions Allowed [§ 4.1-629(B)(2)] • Authorizes localities to adopt ordinances decreasing the VCCA Boardpromulgated minimum distance requirements: • Between Retail Marijuana Stores and Microbusinesses; or • Between a Retail Marijuana Store/Microbusiness and any hospital, public, private or parochial school or institution of higher learning, or child day program 25 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Buffer Distances, con’t Localities may only decrease buffers; they cannot impose stricter distance requirements than those set by the VCCA Board Localities should consider running a GIS suitability analysis (reviewing location of schools, day cares, parks, etc.) before adopting or stacking buffers Overlapping setbacks can unintentionally eliminate all feasible sites in the locality Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 26 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Establish Hours of Sale [§ 4.1-630] 01 02 03 Authorizes cities, towns, and counties of unincorporated areas to adopt ordinances fixing the hours during which cannabis may be sold in the locality Provides any such ordinance shall provide for fine and penalties enforced as a Class 1 misdemeanor, with the right of appeal under § 16.1-106 Once passed, the clerk of the governing body must certify the ordinance and transmit it to the VCCA Board Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 27 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Regulate Hemp/Tobacco Retail Locations [§ 15.2-912.4] Authorizes localities to adopt ordinances regulating the retail sale locations of retail tobacco products or hemp products intended for smoking Localities may prohibit a retail sale location on property within 1,000 linear feet of a child day center or public, private, or parochial schools Deadline for Locality Action: Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 28 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part V: Risk Areas 29 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC De Facto Bans Overly restrictive zoning, buffers, or use-permit denials may be challenged as a de facto ban inconsistent with the statewide marketplace The most defensible ordinances generally: • Identify districts where cannabis uses are permitted • Maintain objective approval criteria • Use traditional zoning standards • Create a record demonstrating reasonable accommodation or licensed cannabis businesses 30 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC By Right vs. SUP and the De Facto Ban Issue • Requiring a special or conditional use permit carries its own preemption risk under § 4.1-629(A) and CAN BECOME A DE FACTO BAN if denials rest on generalized opposition rather than objective planning and safety findings • Objective site development requirements (lighting, screening, security, parking, etc.) generally present lower preemption risk than subjective use-permit denials 31 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC License Objection Process [§ 4.1-810] Upon preliminary license approval, VCCA notifies locality; locality has 30 days to object Objections might include: Failure to object waive local challenge 32 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC •Zoning noncompliance •Land Use violations •Local Ordinance conflicts •Factual errors Litigation Risks De Facto Bans: The locality does not expressly prohibit cannabis use, but it leaves no realistic path to operate within the locality Arbitrary and Capricious Denials: Denials based on generalized concerns about cannabis, or public opposition, rather than objective land use impacts Equal Treatment Claims: Cannabis businesses treated differently than comparable commercial uses without reasonable land use justification 33 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC How Much Zoning is Too Much? A Risk Matrix for Litigation Concerns Lower Risk Moderate Risk Higher Risk Tax Ordinance SUP Requirements No Zoning District Available Hours Ordinance Limited Zoning Districts Excessive Setbacks Objective Site Standards Operational Conditions Repeated Permit Denials Administrative Procedures 34 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Regs That Effectively Prohibit Licensing Part VI: Departmental Checklists 35 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Commissioner of Revenue/Treasurer/Finance 01 02 03 04 05 Establish internal procedures for confirming that cannabis-based applicants are current on their local taxes (§ 4.1900(A)(5)) Build accounting/reconciliation procedures for quarterly state disbursement of “Collections of Local Marijuana Taxes” (§ 4.1614(D)) Update procedures for assessing and collecting BPOL taxes from cannabis businesses Update business license application forms and review procedures for cannabis-specific operations Coordinate with VCCA on tax-rate notices and collection processes 36 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Law Enforcement Develop or update procedures for: • Illegal/unlicensed retail sales operations • Underage possession and use enforcement • Public consumption enforcement • Impaired driving detection and enforcement protocols • Security and crime prevention planning for cash-heavy licensed retail businesses • Evidence handling and chain of custody procedures • Coordination with the VCCA on enforcement investigations • Training and policy updates reflecting the changes to the Virginia law This Photo by Unknown Author is licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 37 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Clerk of the Governing Body Develop procedures related to the Clerk’s responsibilities: • Certify and transmit local ordinances to the VCCA Board (§ 4.1-630) • Notify the VCCA and local retailers within 30 days of the local tax ordinance enactment (§ 4.1-1004) • Track incoming correspondence from the VCCA • Calendar the 30-day objection deadlines for all license applications provided preliminary approval by the VCCA (§ 4.11000(G)) • Designate recipient; create routing protocol; establish legal review timeline; create objection template 38 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Planning and Zoning Applications • Prepare for site plan review submission from license applicants • Establish application procedures • Consider buffer and setback distances 39 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Inspections • Update building and fire inspection procedures for cannabis facilities (ventilation, security, fire suppression, etc.) • Once promulgated, review VCCA’s facility requirements and inspection schedules and develop consistent internal procedures Building and Fire Many local officials have not appreciated risks with cultivation facilities. Consider: • Occupancy classification • Hazardous extraction processes • Ventilation requirements • Odor control • Fire suppression • Security infrastructure 40 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part VII: Inquiring Minds Want to Know 41 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Can the Zoning Administrator Issue Compliance Letters? • Considerations: Has your Zoning Ordinance been amended? • What is the ZA certifying? That marijuana crops are allowed in AG? That retail sales are authorized? How much? To whom? 42 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Must Cannabis Uses be Permitted by Right? • 4.1-629(C) preserves zoning authority • The statute does not expressly require any cannabis use to be permitted by right • However, excessively restrictive zoning could be challenged as inconsistent with 4.1-629(A) • Requiring SUP approval for every cannabis use may create greater litigation risk than permitting some uses by right • No Virginia appellate guidance currently exists 43 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC What Happens if a Locality Does Nothing? • Many local governments are asking: If we take no action, what happens? • Retail cannabis sales remain lawful under state law • VCCA may issue licenses if zoning permits • No local cannabis excise tax will be collected • State hours of sale govern • No local public consumption ordinance exists • Lots of uncertainty for applicants and citizens 44 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Part VIII: Future Issues 45 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC The Next Debate https://cardinalnews.org/2026/08/13/on-a-square-foot-basis-cannabis-growhouses-use-morepower-than-data-centers-why-isnt-their-electricity-use-being-taxed/ 46 | ©2026 Sands Anderson PC Questions? Thank you for your time! title: Notice of Special Called Meeting of the Planning Commission to discuss proposed revisions to the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Ordinance related to solar facilities.
text: COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT botetourtva.gov 57 S. Center Drive Daleville, VA 24083 P: (540) 928-2080 F: (540) 473-2018 NOTICE BOTETOURT COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION The Botetourt County Planning Commission will hold a work session on Monday, December 07, 2026, at 4:00 PM at 57 S. Center Drive, Daleville VA 24083 to discuss proposed revisions to the Comprehensive Plan and the Zoning Ordinance related to solar facilities. While no public hearing or comment period will be held during the work session, the public is welcome to attend. The regular session will follow at 6:00 PM. During the regular 6:00pm session, a public hearing will be held on the following items: Blue Ridge District: Botetourt County Board of Supervisors requests a Rezoning from the Agricultural (A1) Use District to the Business (B-1) Use District with possible proffered conditions as well as a Special Exception Permit for “smaller minimum district sizes in accordance with section 25-224”. The purpose of this project is to expand the existing parking lot and to add outdoor seating for the Blue Ridge branch library. This property totals 2.17 acres, is located at 28 Avery Row, and is identified on Tax Maps as parcel 112-4C. Fincastle District: Calderon Montalvan and Claudia E. Martinez Aguirre request a Special Exception Permit for a Special Events Facility in the Agricultural (A-1) Use District, with possible conditions, in accordance with Sec. 25-73. This property is located at 2457 Gravel Hill Road (US Route 220), Troutville, and is identified on the Tax Maps as parcel 73-168. Amsterdam District: WEBT Holdings, LLC requests a Special Exception Permit, with possible conditions, to increase the number of multi-family dwelling units allowed per acre up to 14.5 dwelling units per acre, in accordance with the Gateway Crossing Overlay District (Community Business Subdistrict), Sec. 25-427 - Uses.
